title.en: US Senate won’t take up ICE funding bill amid row over Trump’s ballroom, which president defends as ‘very good expenditure’ – live
title.zh: 共和党人可能放弃为特朗普宴会厅提供10亿美元的提案——美国政治直播

summary.en: Republican senators have raised concerns about a $1 billion proposal to fund a ballroom for former President Trump, questioning its timing and the lack of detailed information in a bid to add the money to a Department of Homeland Security bill.
summary.zh: 共和党参议员对一项为前总统特朗普的宴会厅提供10亿美元资金的提案表示担忧，质疑其时机以及在试图将这笔资金添加到国土安全部法案中时缺乏细节。

body.en: President claims ‘I don’t need money for the ballroom’ as Senate Republicans move to ditch $1bn funding plan amid fears of alienating voters Sign up for the Breaking News US email Senate Democratic leader Chuck Schumer, House Democratic leader Hakeem Jeffries and other Democrats spoke held a news conference, ahead of the vote-a-rama Thursday morning. “The Republican agenda is one big broken promise,” said Schumer, criticizing the Republican budget bill. “We still haven’t seen the bill, because they are fighting with each other.” Trump v Cook: Donald Trump’s case for firing Federal Reserve governor Lisa Cook, as he continues to exert greater control over the US central bank. Trump v Slaughter: A case which examines the legality of Trump’s firing of a Federal Trade Commission (FTC) member, Rebecca Slaughter. Trump v Barbara: In which the court will decide if the administration’s attempts to restrict birthright citizenship are unconstitutional. Continue reading...
body.zh: 共和党参议员对特勤局为国土安全部法案增加资金的时机和缺乏细节提出质疑。最高法院将于美国东部时间今天上午 10 点发表意见。以下是我们正在密切跟踪的重大案件的提醒。特朗普诉库克：唐纳德·特朗普解雇美联储理事丽莎·库克的理由是，他继续对美联储施加更大的控制。特朗普诉斯劳特：此案审查特朗普解雇联邦贸易委员会 (FTC) 成员丽贝卡·斯劳特的合法性。特朗普诉芭芭拉：法院将决定政府限制出生公民权的尝试是否违宪。继续阅读...

reflection.en: When public funds are involved, integrity and transparency are paramount, reflecting the principle of being trustworthy with what is entrusted to us. The questioning of a significant spending proposal highlights the ongoing need for leaders to be faithful stewards, whether with a little or with much. This vigilance helps ensure that resources are managed...
reflection.zh: 当涉及公共资金时，诚信和透明度至关重要，这反映了对所托付之事忠心负责的原则。对一项重大支出提案的质疑，凸显了领导者无论在小事还是大事上，都需要持续成为忠心的管家。这种警惕有助于确保资源得到负责任的管理，并服务于共同利益。

verse.textEn: Whoever can be trusted with very little can also be trusted with much, and whoever is dishonest with very little will also be dishonest with much.
verse.textZh: 人在最小的事上忠心，在大事上也忠心；在最小的事上不义，在大事上也不义。

title.en: Designs for 250-ft arch in Washington approved by panel of Trump appointees
title.zh: 特朗普任命的委员会批准在华盛顿建造250英尺高的拱门设计

summary.en: A panel of Trump appointees, the Commission of Fine Arts, has approved designs for a 250-foot triumphal arch in Washington D.C., near Arlington National Cemetery. The project has been dubbed 'Arc de Trump'.
summary.zh: 一个由特朗普任命的艺术委员会批准了在华盛顿特区阿灵顿国家公墓附近建造一座250英尺高的凯旋门的设计。该项目被称为“特朗普凯旋门”。

body.en: Approval marks key step forward for project dubbed ‘Arc de Trump’, which will be near Arlington National Cemetery The Commission of Fine Arts on Thursday approved designs for Donald Trump’s proposed 250-ft triumphal arch in Washington DC. The vote on Thursday by the panel, which is made up of Trump appointees, marks a key step forward for the project. Next month, the proposed design is set to be reviewed by the National Capital Planning Commission, another federal panel that oversees planning for federal buildings and land. Continue reading...
body.zh: 批准标志着名为“特朗普凯旋门”的项目向前迈出了关键一步，该项目将在阿灵顿国家公墓附近。美术委员会周四批准了唐纳德·特朗普在华盛顿特区提议的 250 英尺凯旋门的设计。该小组由特朗普任命的人员组成，周四的投票标志着该项目向前迈出了关键一步。下个月，拟议的设计将由国家首都规划委员会审查，该委员会是另一个负责监督联邦建筑和土地规划的联邦小组。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The ambition to build grand structures and 'make a name for ourselves' is a recurring theme in human history, from ancient towers to modern monuments. While human ingenuity can create impressive works, Scripture reminds us that true and lasting significance comes not from self-exaltation, but from a humble recognition of our place before God.
reflection.zh: 从古老的塔楼到现代的纪念碑，建造宏伟建筑并“为自己扬名”是人类历史中反复出现的主题。虽然人类的智慧可以创造令人印象深刻的作品，但圣经提醒我们，真正持久的意义并非来自自我抬高，而是来自谦卑地认识我们在雅伟面前的位置。

verse.textEn: Yahweh said, 'If as one people speaking the same language they have begun to do this, then nothing they plan to do will be impossible for them.'
verse.textZh: 雅伟说：「看哪，他们成为一样的人民，都是一样的言语，如今既做起这事来，以后他们所要做的事就没有不成就的了。」

title.en: Domestic abuse law fails to recognise danger of tech abuse, Lords committee told
title.zh: 上议院委员会被告知：家庭虐待法未能识别技术滥用危险

summary.en: Policy adviser Jen Reed informed a Lords committee that the Domestic Abuse Act does not adequately address technology-facilitated abuse, such as location tracking and hidden stalkerware. She emphasized the increasing prevalence of such abuse and called for its inclusion in the Act.
summary.zh: 政策顾问珍·里德向上议院委员会表示，现行《家庭虐待法》未能充分认识到技术助长型虐待（如位置追踪或隐藏的跟踪软件）的危险。她强调此类虐待日益普遍，并呼吁将其纳入该法案。

body.en: Policy adviser Jen Reed says tech-facilitated abuse has become ‘increasingly prevalent’ and calls for its inclusion in Domestic Abuse Act The Domestic Abuse Act fails to fully recognise the danger of technology-facilitated abuse, such as location tracking or hidden stalkerware, a Lords select committee has heard. Tech abuse has become “increasingly prevalent” and “very commonplace now within a domestic abuse context,” said Jen Reed, the head of policy at University College London’s Gender and Tech Research Lab, during an evidence session. Continue reading...
body.zh: 政策顾问珍·里德 (Jen Reed) 表示，技术辅助的虐待行为已变得“越来越普遍”，并呼吁将其纳入《家庭虐待法》。上议院特别委员会获悉，《家庭虐待法》未能充分认识到技术辅助的虐待行为的危险，例如位置跟踪或隐藏的跟踪软件。伦敦大学学院性别与技术研究实验室政策负责人珍·里德在一次证据会议上表示，科技滥用已经变得“越来越普遍”，并且“在家庭暴力的背景下非常普遍”。继续阅读...

reflection.en: The call to "seek justice" and "correct oppression" reminds us of our responsibility to protect the vulnerable, especially when new forms of harm emerge. As technology evolves, so must our legal and social frameworks to ensure safety for those experiencing domestic abuse. This story highlights the ongoing need for vigilance and advocacy to adapt laws that...
reflection.zh: “寻求公正，纠正欺压”的呼召提醒我们有责任保护弱势群体，尤其当新的伤害形式出现时。随着科技发展，我们的法律和社会框架也必须随之调整，以确保家庭虐待受害者的安全。这个故事凸显了持续警惕和倡导的重要性，以修订法律来捍卫受欺压者。

verse.textEn: Learn to do right; seek justice. Defend the oppressed. Take up the cause of the fatherless; plead the case of the widow.
verse.textZh: 学习行善，寻求公平，解救受欺压的；给孤儿伸冤，为寡妇辨屈。

title.en: Single sex toilets must exclude transgender people, says EHRC
title.zh: 英国平等与人权委员会称单性别厕所必须排除跨性别者

summary.en: A new code of practice issued by the Equality and Human Rights Commission (EHRC) for England, Wales, and Scotland states that single-sex toilets and changing rooms must exclude transgender men and women. This guidance follows a supreme court ruling and also covers changing facilities.
summary.zh: 英国平等与人权委员会（EHRC）为英格兰、威尔士和苏格兰发布的新行为准则规定，单性别厕所和更衣室必须排除跨性别男性和女性。该指南遵循最高法院的裁决，也适用于更衣设施。

body.en: Updated code of practice covering England, Wales and Scotland also relates to changing rooms and follows supreme court ruling Single-sex toilets and changing rooms in England, Wales and Scotland must exclude transgender men and women, according to a new code of practice from the equalities watchdog. But the long-awaited guidance also says that businesses and service providers have to offer practical alternatives such as gender-neutral toilets for people who do not wish to use services for their biological sex. title.en: Pair arrested after boys abandoned by road in Portugal
title.zh: 葡萄牙男孩被遗弃在公路上，两人被捕

summary.en: The children were carrying backpacks with food and water but no identity documents when they were found by a driver.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及公义、尊严与问责。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The mother and stepfather of two young French boys found alone and in tears by the side of a road in southern Portugal have been arrested.

The children - both under five - were found by a driver near the town of Alcacer do Sal on Tuesday, police said.

The boys' father had reported them missing from their home in Colmar in eastern France on 11 May and France had issued a pan-European request for help.

Police in Portugal and France have opened inquiries and said they had not reached any conclusions at this stage.

Local media reports said the couple were arrested after their car was spotted outside a café in the city of Fatima, about 180km (112 miles) north of Alcacer do Sal.

Portugal's National Republican Guard said its officers arrested a 41-year-old woman and man aged 55. They have not formally identified the arrested pair.

They said the couple were being investigated for the crimes of domestic violence, exposure to danger, and abandonment.
body.zh: 两名法国小男孩的母亲和继父被发现独自在葡萄牙南部的一条路边哭泣，现已被捕。 警方称，周二，一名司机在阿尔卡塞尔杜萨尔镇附近发现了这两个五岁以下的孩子。 5 月 11 日，男孩的父亲报告称他们在法国东部科尔马的家中失踪，法国已向全欧洲发出求助请求。 葡萄牙和法国警方已展开调查，并表示现阶段尚未得出任何结论。 当地媒体报道称，这对夫妇在法蒂玛市一家咖啡馆外发现他们的汽车后被捕，该市位于萨尔堡以北约 180 公里（112 英里）处。 葡萄牙国家共和卫队表示，其官员逮捕了一名 41 岁的女子和一名 55 岁的男子。他们尚未正式确认被捕的两人的身份。 他们表示，这对夫妇因家庭暴力、暴露于危险和遗弃等罪名正在接受调查。

title.en: Walmart warns US shoppers are cutting spending as higher petrol prices bite
title.zh: 沃尔玛警告美国消费者因汽油价格上涨而削减开支

summary.en: The retail giant Walmart has issued a warning that American consumers are expected to reduce their spending in the coming months, primarily due to the impact of higher gasoline prices.
summary.zh: 零售巨头沃尔玛警告称，由于汽油价格上涨的影响，预计美国消费者在未来几个月将削减开支。

body.en:
Walmart has warned higher petrol prices are causing US consumers to cut spending elsewhere as the war with Iran continues to squeeze household budgets.

The retail giant expects its sales growth between May and July to slow significantly from the previous three months, with higher prices at the pump to blame.

The conflict in the Middle East has led to a surge in wholesale oil prices, in turn pushing up the price of petrol for Americans .

Data from motoring group AAA shows the average price of a gallon of petrol has hit $4.56 (£3.40), up from $3 when the war began.

In an interview with CNBC, Walmart finance boss John David Rainey said the rising cost of living had so far been offset by higher tax returns as a result of tax cuts in President Donald Trump's One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBBA).

But he warned shoppers would be under increasing strain as that effect drains away in its current financial quarter.

"I think higher tax returns muted some of the pressure related to higher fuel prices and as we're in a period of time right now where those tax refunds are largely not coming in, I think consumers are going to feel more of that pressure from higher fuel prices," he said.

The retailer was "keeping a close eye" on petrol prices but expects them to remain high for the coming months, Rainey said.

Walmart is the biggest private employer in the US and one of its biggest retailers, so its earnings offer an insight into how American consumers are being affected by the fallout from the Iran war.

On a call with investors, Rainey also warned that if the closure of the Strait of Hormuz continues, it could force the retailer to hike food prices due to shortages of fertiliser, nitrogen and phosphates.

Walmart's first-quarter profit, from February to April, was $5.3bn, up 18.8% compared with a year earlier.

But it warned this rate of growth would slow to between 4% and 5% between May and July as the rising cost of living begins to bite.

The company's shares fell by 7% on Thursday morning in response to the worse-than-expected guidance.

AJ Bell's head of financial analysis, Danni Hewson, said Walmart's warning highlighted the impact of the fuel shock on consumer spending power in the US.

"But a consumer facing their own rising fuel costs will continue to seek out the kind of value that Walmart has become synonymous with after a series of price cuts beginning last year," she added.
body.zh: 沃尔玛警告称，由于与伊朗的战争继续挤压家庭预算，汽油价格上涨导致美国消费者削减其他地方的支出。 这家零售巨头预计 5 月至 7 月的销售增长将比前三个月大幅放缓，原因是油价上涨。 中东冲突导致批发石油价格飙升，进而推高了美国人的汽油价格。 汽车集团 AAA 的数据显示，每加仑汽油的平均价格已从战争开始时的 3 美元上涨至 4.56 美元（3.40 英镑）。 沃尔玛财务负责人约翰·戴维·雷尼 (John David Rainey) 在接受 CNBC 采访时表示，迄今为止，生活成本的上涨已被唐纳德·特朗普总统的一项美丽法案 (OBBBA) 减税带来的更高的纳税申报所抵消。 但他警告说，随着这种影响在当前财务季度逐渐消失，购物者将面临越来越大的压力。 他说：“我认为较高的纳税申报表减轻了与燃油价格上涨相关的一些压力，而且由于目前我们正处于退税基本上没有到位的时期，我认为消费者将感受到燃油价格上涨带来的更大压力。” 雷尼表示，该零售商正在“密切关注”汽油价格，但预计未来几个月油价将保持在高位。 沃尔玛是美国最大的私人雇主，也是最大的零售商之一，因此其收益可以让我们了解美国消费者如何受到伊朗战争影响。 雷尼在与投资者的电话会议上还警告说，如果霍尔木兹海峡的关闭继续下去，可能会迫使零售商因化肥、氮肥和磷酸盐的短缺而提高食品价格。 沃尔玛2月至4月第一季度利润为53亿美元，同比增长18.8%。 但它警告说，随着生活成本上升开始产生影响，5 月至 7 月期间这一增长率将放缓至 4% 至 5%。 由于业绩指引差于预期，该公司股价周四上午下跌 7%。

reflection.en: As rising petrol prices compel households to cut back on spending, many face the challenge of making do with less. This situation reminds us that true contentment isn't solely dependent on material abundance, but can be found even amidst scarcity.
reflection.zh: 随着汽油价格上涨迫使家庭削减开支，许多人面临着节衣缩食的挑战。这提醒我们，真正的满足感并非完全取决于物质的丰盛，即使在匮乏之中也能找到。

verse.textEn: Though the fig tree does not bud and there are no grapes on the vines... yet I will rejoice in Yahweh.
verse.textZh: 虽然无花果树不发旺，葡萄树不结果……然而，我要因雅伟欢欣。

title.en: DR Congo cancels World Cup training camp over Ebola outbreak
title.zh: 刚果民主共和国因埃博拉疫情取消世界杯训练营

summary.en: The outbreak, caused by a rare Ebola species, is thought to have caused 139 deaths so far.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及受造之物关怀与环保责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The Democratic Republic of Congo has cancelled its pre-World Cup training camp in the capital, Kinshasa, because of an Ebola outbreak in the east of the country.

The virus is thought to have killed more than 130, including a person whose case was confirmed on Thursday in the South Kivu province, signalling the spread of the virus from the outbreak's epicentre.

The World Health Organization (WHO) has called the outbreak a "public health emergency of international concern", but said it was not at pandemic level.

A spokesperson for DR Congo's football team told reporters that the training camp, part of the preparations for the team's first World Cup since 1974, would now take place in Belgium.

Jerry Kalemo added that DR Congo's pre-tournament games in Europe would go ahead as planned.

The Leopards are due to play friendly matches against Denmark, on 3 June in Belgium, and Chile, on 9 June in Spain, ahead of the World Cup finals.

They play their first match of the tournament in the US city of Houston on 17 June against Portugal.

"Originally scheduled to take place in the capital on May 26, the Leopards' public training session will not be held after all. This decision follows reports of suspected Ebola cases in the provinces of North Kivu and Ituri," a message posted by the team on social media said.

There is also uncertainty over whether the team's French coach, Sébastien Desabre, will go ahead with a press conference scheduled to take place in the capital city, the statement added.

A spokesperson for the DR Congo team told the Reuters news agency that the training camp had been cancelled due to travel restrictions imposed by the US, who are hosting the World Cup this summer, along with Mexico and Canada.

All DR Congo's players are based outside the central African country and will therefore not be affected by the restrictions now the training camp has been cancelled.

Some team staff based in DR Congo left the country on Wednesday, Kalemo told the Associated Press, ahead of the 21-day deadline.

summary.en: An outbreak of Ebola in DR Congo involves a rare species of the virus and is in an area affected by conflict.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
An Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of Congo has been declared a public health emergency of international concern, by the World Health Organization (WHO).

The latest outbreak is challenging because it involves a rare species of Ebola for which there is no vaccine, and the epicentre is in an area affected by conflict.

The WHO has told the BBC that the outbreak may be spreading faster than originally thought.

Ebola viruses normally infect animals, typically fruit bats, but outbreaks among humans can sometimes start when people eat or handle infected animals.

It takes two to 21 days for symptoms to appear. They come on suddenly and start like the flu or malaria, with fever, headache and tiredness.

As the disease progresses, vomiting and diarrhoea develop and it can lead to organ failure. Some, but not all, patients develop internal and external bleeding.

The virus spreads from one person to another by contact with infected bodily fluids such as blood or vomit.

Ebola outbreaks used to be small and contained to remote rural areas. However, urbanisation is pushing larger populations closer to these natural reservoirs of Ebola and increasing the risk of transmission.

This outbreak is caused by the rare Bundibugyo species of Ebola, which had not been seen for over a decade.

Named after a district in Uganda where it was first detected, Bundibugyo has only caused two previous outbreaks - in 2007 and 2012.

One study showed that it killed about a third of those infected, far less than the more common Zaire (66.6%) and Sudan (48.5%) species.

Initial blood tests for Ebola in the affected areas were negative as they were designed to identify the more common species of the disease.

There is no approved vaccine for Bundibugyo, but experimental ones are in development. It is possible that a vaccine for the Zaire species may offer some protection.

A further complication is that the outbreak is taking place in a conflict zone, with a quarter of million people displaced from their homes and people moving across porous borders into neighbouring countries.

Trish Newport, from medical charity Doctors Without Borders, who is heavily involved in efforts to tackle the outbreak, told the BBC World Service that territory constantly changed hands between different armed groups, making it difficult for emergency response teams to simply drive to Ebola hot-spots.

She pointed out that a further problem was bad roads, with a 90km (56-mile) journey from Bunia city to Mongwalu, one of two gold-mining towns where the majority of cases have been reported, taking more than three hours.

Newport added that for Mongwalu's residents, the Ebola outbreak was a "very scary moment".

body.en:
Saudi Arabia has been directly hit by missiles and drones during the Iran war, but the country is hosting the all-important Muslim pilgrimage anyway.

This year is the first time that Saudi Arabia has chosen to go ahead with the annual Hajj pilgrimage while it is also in the middle of a war that has seen direct strikes on Saudi territory.

The Hajj is a once-a-year event that draws millions of Muslims to Mecca in Saudi Arabia to perform rituals that every believer is supposed to carry out at least once in their lives, if they are able to. It is one of the largest gatherings of humans worldwide, and this year's Hajj runs between May 25 and May 29 with around 1.5 million pilgrims expected in Saudi Arabia. Over the past three years, between 1.7 and 1.8 million have attended.

Historians say that over 14 centuries, the Hajj has only ever been canceled or restricted about 40 times; the last time that happened was during the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020.

Having more than a million pilgrims descend upon one place to perform the same ritual in under a week has always been a complex logistical exercise . It has involved Saudi Arabia restricting crowds with a ticket lottery  system for international pilgrims, tight security at pilgrimage sites, flights, accommodation, food and water and medical care, and all that amid  high temperatures that have proven deadly in the past.

This year that exercise is being complicated by the Iran war , which began in late February when the US and Israel attacked Iran. Iran has responded by targeting the Gulf states, along with Israel.

There is a ceasefire in effect at the moment but it remains unclear how steady that is. Last weekend, Saudi Arabia intercepted three drones it says were likely launched by pro-Iran militias in Iraq.

2026 also marks the first time the US government has urged its own citizens to reconsider participating in the pilgrimage, noting that "non-emergency US government employees were ordered to leave Saudi Arabia" in early March.

Germany, the United Kingdom and other European nations have also issued travel warnings for Saudi Arabia, strongly advising citizens against going there during the current conflict or if they do, then to monitor the situation closely. Several travel agencies in Germany that specialize in Hajj travel did not reply to DW's inquiries about how would-be pilgrims were reacting to those sorts of warnings.

title.en: Russia and China condemn US over indictment of former Cuban leader
title.zh: 俄罗斯和中国谴责美国起诉古巴前领导人

summary.en: The United States has charged former Cuban leader Raúl Castro with murder, a move that has drawn condemnation from Russia and China. This action is the latest in efforts by the US to exert pressure on the Cuban regime.
summary.zh: 美国指控古巴前领导人劳尔·卡斯特罗犯有谋杀罪，此举遭到俄罗斯和中国的谴责。这是美国向古巴政权施压的最新举措。

body.en:
China and Russia have condemned a US decision to charge Cuba's former president Raúl Castro with murder.

The Chinese foreign ministry called on the US to stop using "coercion" and "threats" against its ally, while the Kremlin said the pressure being exerted on Havana "borders on violence".

The US has accused Castro over the 1996 downing of two planes, an incident that killed four people and fuelled diplomatic tensions between Washington and the Caribbean island.

US President Donald Trump has repeatedly sought to exert pressure on Cuba and has openly discussed toppling its communist regime.

The US has imposed fresh sanctions on the country and imposed an effective blockade on oil shipments to Cuba, exacerbating a fuel crisis there and leading to extended blackouts and food shortages.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media on Thursday that the US pressure campaign against Russia's long-time ally, including the indictment Castro, "cannot be condoned".

"We believe that under no circumstances should such methods - which border on violence - be used against either former or current heads of state," he added.

Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun had earlier said the US should "stop threatening force at every turn", and that Beijing "firmly supports Cuba".

He said Beijing opposed "any attempt by external forces to exert pressure on Cuba under any pretext".

Guo continued: "The United States should cease using sanctions and judicial apparatus as tools of coercion against Cuba and refrain from making threats of force at every turn."

Castro was charged alongside five others on Wednesday over their alleged involvement in the shooting down of the two planes, which had been travelling between Cuba and Florida when they were struck.

The aircraft, which were operated by the Cuban-American dissident group Brothers to the Rescue, had been carrying three US citizens when they were downed, all of whom were killed.

At the time, Castro - who stepped down as president in 2018 - was head of the country's armed forces.

The incident caused outcry among Cuban exiles living in the US and has long been a source of contention between Washington and Havana.

Cuba's President Miguel Díaz-Canel has described the charges as "a political manoeuvre, devoid of any legal foundation".

Since capturing former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January, Trump has openly mused that Cuba was "ready to fall" .

It was a federal indictment against the left-wing authoritarian Maduro that was used by the Trump administration as its justification for its raid on the Venezuelan capital, Caracas, to seize him and his wife, Cilia Flores. The pair are now due to stand trial in New York on charges including drug trafficking.

title.zh: 捷克：布尔诺苏台德德国集会引起轩然大波

summary.en: The first gathering of Sudeten Germans in Czechia since World War II is set to go ahead this weekend despite a political backlash that has exposed tensions over one of Central Europe's most painful historical legacies.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
The first gathering of Sudeten Germans in Czechia since World War II is set to go ahead this weekend despite a political backlash that has exposed tensions over one of Central Europe's most painful historical legacies.

The annual Sudetendeutscher Tag, a meeting of ethnic Germans expelled from Czechoslovakia after the Second World War and their descendants, will take place in the Czech city of Brno from May 22 to 25 as part of the Meeting Brno festival of reconciliation.

But the event has triggered protests and a parliamentary declaration warning against what some Czech lawmakers called "historical revisionism" and the "relativization of Nazi crimes."

"The Chamber of Deputies expresses its opposition to the holding of the 76th convention of the Sudetendeutsche Landsmannschaft [Sudeten German Association] on the territory of the Czech Republic , in view of the historical context and the fact that attitudes questioning the postwar settlement have long appeared within parts of this movement," read the declaration passed in the lower house of the Czech parliament on Friday.

The motion, which was symbolic and non-binding, passed by 73 votes to none, with four abstentions.

Center-right opposition parties boycotted the debate, accusing the governing coalition — which includes the far-right SPD party — of exploiting the issue for political gain.

Prime Minister Andrej Babis has apparently changed his stance on the event. He recently said that the gathering in Brno is "not a fortunate development" despite having previously referred to it in neutral terms as a civic initiative that the Czech government was not dealing with.

The event has also drawn protests in Brno itself. Around 500 people joined a demonstration in April organized by the SPD.

The SPD is firmly opposed to the gathering and accuses Sudeten German organizations of seeking to overturn the postwar Benes decrees that confiscated German property and stripped ethnic Germans of citizenship.

This accusation is rejected by Bernd Posselt, chairman of the Sudeten German Association, the main organization representing Sudeten German expellees. Posselt has stressed that the Sudeten German Association no longer seeks to challenge the postwar order and described the event as an effort at reconciliation.

In 2015, the association made some key changes to its charter , among other things removing references to reparations and the reclamation of land.

Posselt, a former MEP for Bavaria's conservative Christian Social Union, told DW that the organization wanted an honest discussion of the past. He has since criticized the parliamentary declaration and insisted the gathering would go ahead.

body.zh: 尽管政治上的强烈反对暴露了中欧最痛苦的历史遗产之一的紧张局势，但二战以来苏台德德国人在捷克的首次集会仍将在本周末举行。 一年一度的苏台德意志大会（Sudetendeutscher Tag）是二战后被驱逐出捷克斯洛伐克的德意志人及其后裔的一次聚会，将于 5 月 22 日至 25 日在捷克布尔诺市举行，作为布尔诺和解节的一部分。 但这一事件引发了抗议活动，议会发表声明警告一些捷克议员所谓的“历史修正主义”和“纳粹罪行的相对化”。 捷克议会下院周五通过的声明中写道：“考虑到历史背景以及该运动部分地区长期以来存在质疑战后解决方案的态度，众议院表示反对在捷克共和国境内举行苏台德德国协会第76届代表大会。” 该动议具有象征性，不具约束力，以 73 票对零票、四票弃权获得通过。 中右翼反对党抵制这场辩论，指责包括极右翼社会民主党在内的执政联盟利用这一问题谋取政治利益。 总理安德烈·巴比斯显然改变了对这一事件的立场。他最近表示，布尔诺的集会“并不是一个幸运的事态发展”，尽管他之前曾用中性的措辞将其称为捷克政府没有处理的公民倡议。 该事件还引起了布尔诺本身的抗议。大约 500 人参加了社民党 4 月份组织的示威活动。 社会民主党坚决反对这次集会，并指责苏台德德国组织试图推翻战后没收德国财产并剥夺德国人公民身份的贝奈斯法令。 代表苏台德德国被驱逐者的主要组织苏台德德国协会主席伯恩德·波塞尔特驳斥了这一指控。波塞尔特强调，苏台德德国协会不再寻求挑战战后秩序，并将此次活动描述为和解的努力。 2015年，该协会对其章程进行了一些重大修改，其中删除了有关赔偿和开垦土地的内容。 巴伐利亚保守基督教社会联盟前欧洲议会议员波塞尔特告诉德国之声，该组织希望对过去进行诚实的讨论。此后他批评了议会的声明，并坚称集会将继续进行。 布尔诺会议节的组织者还发表声明称，聚会将按以下方式进行：

title.en: Turkey: DW's Alican Uludag released, but trial continues
title.zh: 土耳其：德国之声的 Alican Uludag 获释，但审判仍在继续

summary.en: A Turkish court has allowed DW reporter Alican Uludag to leave detention as his contentious trial opens. He is accused of having "insulted" President Recep Tayyip Erdogan, which in Turkey can carry a jail sentence.

title.en: New Chinese surveillance leaves foreigners nowhere to hide
title.zh: 中国新的监控让外国人无处藏身

summary.en: A Chinese cybersecurity expert has revealed to DW details of China's new high-tech policing. From ski resort facial recognition to seats on a train, the system can track anyone and compile a "holistic profile."
summary.zh: 这是一则来自全球栏目的新闻，重点涉及真理、分辨与诚实。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
A Chinese cybersecurity expert has revealed to DW details of China's new high-tech policing. From ski resort facial recognition to seats on a train, the system can track anyone and compile a "holistic profile."

When a cybersecurity researcher known by the pseudonym NetAskari recently clicked on a tab labeled "Inquiry for journalist files" on an unsecured Chinese web dashboard, he expected to see a jumble of auto-generated mock data.

Instead, familiar faces popped up on the screen. It was a comprehensive database of almost every foreign journalist based in the Chinese capital Beijing around 2021, including official passport photos taken at the entry/exit bureau, private cell phone numbers, visa details, and dates of birth. He also found his own exact personal information lying dormant on this Chinese police watchlist.

"It was more interesting than shocking," NetAskari told DW. "When you work as a journalist in China , you basically assume you are always on their radar. But what surprised me was simply how easy it was to access this highly sensitive system."

What NetAskari had stumbled upon is part modern China's emerging system of "holographic profiles."

He had unwittingly accessed a demonstration version of a remote tracking system designed for the Public Security Bureau in Zhangjiakou, the Hebei province city that hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics.

Though it was only a test panel, it was populated with real datasets, clearly outlining the trajectory of China's state surveillance machine, which is rapidly evolving from a network of simple street cameras into a data-fused, 24/7, predictive social control behemoth.

For years, China has operated the world's most extensive CCTV network. A massive initiative known as the "Xueliang" (Bright Eyes) project aims to merge these isolated islands of surveillance spread across the country.

But the data on the Zhangjiakou police dashboard shows the granular detail with which authorities can track an individual.

This system no longer relies solely on police cameras on street corners. It accurately records the specific train carriage and seat number a target occupies when arriving from Beijing or Shanghai.

It even synchronizes photos taken by facial-recognition ticket gates at local ski resorts directly into its tracking mechanism. The movements of the researcher's acquaintances who recently skied in Zhangjiakou were precisely flagged and mapped out with detailed trajectories in the system.

"The idea is simply to process as much data as possible from as many sensors as possible in real time," the researcher noted.

The system logs daily behaviors like gasoline consumption, regular shopping locations, and whether an individual frequently visits "petition areas."

body.zh: 一位中国网络安全专家向德国之声透露了中国新型高科技警务的细节。从滑雪场面部识别到火车座位，该系统可以跟踪任何人并编制“整体档案”。 当一位化名 NetAskari 的网络安全研究人员最近点击一个不安全的中文网络仪表板上标有“查询记者档案”的选项卡时，他预计会看到一堆自动生成的模拟数据。 取而代之的是，熟悉的面孔出现在屏幕上。这是 2021 年左右驻扎在中国首都北京的几乎所有外国记者的综合数据库，包括在出入境管理局拍摄的官方护照照片、私人手机号码、签证详细信息和出生日期。他还发现自己的确切个人信息隐藏在中国警方的监视名单上。 “这比令人震惊更有趣，”内特阿斯卡里告诉德国之声。 “当你在中国担任记者时，你基本上会认为你总是在他们的监视范围内。但令我惊讶的是访问这个高度敏感的系统是多么容易。” NetAskari 偶然发现的是现代中国新兴的“全息轮廓”系统的一部分。 他无意中访问了为主办 2022 年冬季奥运会的河北省张家口市公安局设计的远程跟踪系统演示版本。 虽然它只是一个测试面板，但它填充了真实的数据集，清楚地概述了中国国家监控机器的轨迹，该机器正在从简单的街道摄像头网络迅速演变为数据融合的、24/7、预测性的社会控制庞然大物。 多年来，中国运营着世界上最广泛的闭路电视网络。一项名为“雪亮”（明亮的眼睛）项目的大规模倡议旨在合并这些分布在全国各地的监视孤岛。 但张家口警方仪表板上的数据显示了当局可以追踪个人的详细信息。 该系统不再仅仅依赖街角的警察摄像头。它准确记录目标从北京或上海到达时所占用的具体火车车厢和座位号。 它甚至将当地滑雪场的面部识别检票口拍摄的照片直接同步到其跟踪机制中。研究人员最近在张家口滑雪的熟人的动作被精确标记，并在系统中绘制出详细的轨迹。 研究人员指出：“这个想法只是实时处理来自尽可能多的传感器的尽可能多的数据。” 该系统记录日常行为，例如汽油消耗、常规购物地点以及个人是否经常访问“请愿区”。 这项大规模的数据融合工作试图……

title.en: Australian activists detained by Israel set to be released
title.zh: 以色列拘留的澳大利亚活动人士将获释

summary.en: Australian activists who were detained by Israel are now scheduled for release and deportation. This development follows a period of global controversy sparked by a video posted on X by Israel's police minister.

body.en:
A group of Australians taken by Israel while trying to deliver aid to Gaza are set to be released from detention.

Eleven Australians were among 400 people taking part in the Global Sumud Flotilla to Gaza before being intercepted by Israeli forces at gunpoint in international waters on Tuesday.

In a statement on Thursday night, the Australian Delegation for Global Sumud Flotilla said the Australians were being taken by bus to Ramon Airport in Israel, where they were expected to board flights bound for Istanbul, Türkiye.

Earlier, Israel's ambassador to Australia Hillel Newman said the activists were "certainly safe", had access to consular officials and would be deported following due process.

"No one is in harm's way ... the dealing with them was very sensitive," he told reporters in Canberra on Thursday.

The treatment of the activists by police officers under Israel's police minister Itamar Ben-Gvir's direction drew an international outcry and a rebuke from Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

Ben-Gvir and at least one other minister ‌in Netanyahu's government, transport chief Miri Regev, posted campaign-style videos of themselves visiting the port and lambasting the protesters, attention-grabbing antics before potential early elections in Israel.

Flotilla organisers say they aim to break Israel's blockade of Gaza by delivering humanitarian assistance, something aid bodies say is still in short supply despite a US-brokered ceasefire between Israel and Hamas in place since October 2025 that includes guarantees of increased aid.

The flotilla departed from southern Türkiye this week before being intercepted on Wednesday.

Past flotillas — including one carrying Swedish activist Greta Thunberg — were also ‌intercepted by Israel, with participants ‌later deported.

In a statement, Israeli ⁠rights group Adalah said the estimated 430 activists had been released from prison in southern Israel and would be deported on Thursday via the Ramon airport near Eilat on the Red Sea.

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan said his country was conducting special flights that'd bring Turkish citizens as well as third-country participants to Türkiye.

Those on board the flotilla included citizens of Spain, South Korea and Ireland.

"We will continue to uphold the rights of our citizens and fulfil our humanitarian responsibility toward civilians in Gaza," Fidan said.

Spain's foreign minister said its diplomats in Israel had been informed that some 44 Spanish flotilla members would depart from Israel in the mid-afternoon.

title.zh: “大三角”逆转：习近平会见特朗普，然后是普京。这表明世界可能正在发生转变

summary.en: The Chinese president held meetings with two global leaders, one focused on economic agreements and the other on geopolitical tensions, indicating a potential shift in international dynamics.
summary.zh: 中国国家主席与两位全球领导人举行了会晤，其中一次会议侧重于经济协议，另一次则聚焦于地缘政治对抗，这预示着国际格局可能正在发生转变。

body.en:
Peking duck, Chinese opera and Tchaikovsky's Swan Lake — this was Chinese leader Xi Jinping's grand welcome for his "old friend", Russian President Vladimir Putin.

"Not seeing you for one day feels like being apart for three autumns," Putin told Xi, a saying from one of China's oldest poetry collections, as they met in Beijing.

The friendly exchange took place in the Great Hall of the People, an imposing building on Tiananmen Square that houses China's legislature, the same spot where United States President Donald Trump stood less than a week ago .

The timing of the back-to-back meetings might have been coincidental, as Trump postponed an earlier summit in March to stay in the US during the war in Iran.

"These two visits reveal a deeper structural shift in global politics," Alexander Korolev, senior lecturer in politics and international relations at UNSW Sydney, told SBS News.

"China, I think, is increasingly becoming the central node ... We can call it a great triangle reversed, or we can probably call it a great triangle with Chinese characteristics.

"During the Cold War, the United States was the apex of the great triangle, but now it is flipped, and China is sitting at the top of the triangle," he said.

"It's not that China is trying to put Washington and Moscow against each other, but it's increasingly positioning itself as the centre of the system, the place where major power diplomacy must pass."

Putin's meeting with Xi did not go entirely as the Russians would likely have hoped, as he failed to secure a deal for the Power of Siberia 2 pipeline, which will transport gas from Siberia to China if it goes ahead.

Russian officials said both sides had reached a "general understanding on the parameters" of the project.

The leaders also issued a joint statement, outlining plans to expand collaboration across various fields, from artificial intelligence to the conservation of rare species such as tigers, leopards, and pandas.

Edward Chan, a postdoctoral fellow of China Studies at the Australian National University, said the meeting "is likely to underscore continuity in the China–Russia relationship".

"Xi wanted to remain committed to its partnership with Putin. This was reflected in the joint statement, which continued to emphasise the China–Russia comprehensive strategic partnership of coordination," he told SBS News.

"In that sense, the meeting was seen more as a reaffirmation of the China–Russia relationship amid the US–China stabilised great power relationship."

Xi and Putin also criticised Trump's Golden Dome missile defence shield — a space-based missile interceptor system.

body.zh: 北京烤鸭、中国戏曲、柴可夫斯基的《天鹅湖》——这是中国领导人习近平对“老朋友”俄罗斯总统普京的隆重欢迎。 普京在北京会面时对习近平说：“一日不见，犹如三秋别离。”这是中国最古老的诗集之一中的一句话。 这次友好交流是在人民大会堂举行的，这是一座位于天安门广场上的宏伟建筑，是中国立法机关的所在地，不到一周前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普也曾站过这里。 连续举行会议的时间可能纯属巧合，因为特朗普推迟了三月份的峰会，以便在伊朗战争期间留在美国。 “这两次访问揭示了全球政治更深层次的结构性转变，”悉尼新南威尔士大学政治和国际关系高级讲师亚历山大·科罗廖夫告诉SBS新闻。 “我认为，中国正在日益成为中心节点……我们可以称之为倒转大三角，也可以称之为具有中国特色的大三角。 他说：“冷战期间，美国是大三角的顶点，但现在它翻转了，中国坐在三角的顶端。” “中国并不是试图让华盛顿和莫斯科相互对立，而是越来越将自己定位为体系的中心，是大国外交的必经之地。” 普京与习近平的会晤并没有完全像俄罗斯人希望的那样进行，因为他未能就西伯利亚力量2号管道达成协议，该管道如果顺利进行，将把天然气从西伯利亚输送到中国。 俄罗斯官员表示，双方已就该项目的“参数达成总体谅解”。 领导人还发表了联合声明，概述了扩大各个领域合作的计划，从人工智能到保护老虎、豹子和熊猫等稀有物种。 澳大利亚国立大学中国研究博士后研究员爱德华·陈表示，这次会议“可能会强调中俄关系的连续性”。 “习近平希望继续致力于与普京的伙伴关系。这在联合声明中得到了体现，联合声明继续强调中俄全面战略协作伙伴关系，”他告诉SBS新闻。 “从这个意义上说，这次会晤更多地被视为在美中稳定的大国关系中对中俄关系的重申。” 习近平和普京还批评了特朗普的金顶导弹防御系统——一种天基导弹拦截系统。 近一周前，特朗普将习近平描述为“伟大的领导人”，并表示很“荣幸”……

title.en: Australia endorses historic UN resolution for climate change accountability
title.zh: 澳大利亚支持联合国具有历史意义的气候变化问责决议

summary.en: Australia voted to endorse a UN advisory opinion on climate change accountability, despite being a major global exporter of coal and gas.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚投票支持联合国关于气候变化问责制的咨询意见，尽管该国是全球主要的煤炭和天然气出口国之一。

body.en:
Australia has voted in favour of a landmark United Nations resolution, spearheaded by its Pacific island neighbours, urging action on climate change.

The 193-member global body endorsed an advisory opinion provided by the International Court of Justice (ICJ) on Wednesday, which notably warns that the failure to curb fossil fuel production could constitute an "internationally wrongful act".

The hard-fought legal opinion from the world's top court , delivered in July 2025, was first conceived by a group of Pacific students.

The Pacific island nation of Vanuatu was the first to act in support of the opinion.

The climate-vulnerable island nation, supported by its Pacific allies, was also the first to sponsor the UN General Assembly resolution.

The resolution passed with 141 votes in favour, eight against and 28 abstentions.

Pacific Islands Students Fighting Climate Change director Vishal Prasad is one of the students who instigated the ICJ advisory opinion.

"This must be a turning point in accountability for damaging the climate," he said.

"Communities on the frontlines, like in the Pacific, have been waiting far too long and continue to pay too high a price for the actions of others."

Amanda McKenzie, chief executive of the Australia-based Climate Council, said the ruling exposes the federal government's stance on fossil fuel exports.

"While the government is ramping up renewable power, it is still giving fossil fuel giants a free ride," she said.

"Continuing to wave through massive new coal and gas projects puts our kids' future at risk and is now clearly against international law."

The nation remains a major exporter of coal and gas, despite pursuing significant domestic emissions cuts and ambitious renewables targets.

Other big fossil fuel producers, including the United States, Russia, Iran and Saudi Arabia, opposed the measure.

Australia was not among the resolution's 69 co-sponsors leading into the vote. Australia and New Zealand were the only Pacific nations missing from the list.

Australia holds a key president of negotiations role heading into the next Conference of the Parties climate change talks to be held in Türkiye, with Fiji and Tuvalu set to hold official pre-event meetings.

Low-lying Tuvalu is expected to lose 90 per cent of its land to the ocean by the end of the century due to sea level rise.

The UN General Assembly resolution formally reaffirms the ICJ's findings and urges governments to align policies with limiting global warming to 1.5C.

It also urges nations in violation to provide reparation for damage and calls for the regulation of fossil fuel companies.

body.zh: 澳大利亚投票赞成由其太平洋岛屿邻国牵头的一项具有里程碑意义的联合国决议，敦促采取行动应对气候变化。 这个拥有 193 个成员国的全球机构周三认可了国际法院 (ICJ) 提供的咨询意见，该意见特别警告说，未能遏制化石燃料生产可能构成“国际不法行为”。 世界最高法院于 2025 年 7 月发表的经过艰苦斗争的法律意见，最初是由一群太平洋学生提出的。 太平洋岛国瓦努阿图最先表态支持这一观点。 这个气候脆弱的岛国在其太平洋盟友的支持下，也是第一个提出联合国大会决议的国家。 该决议以 141 票赞成、8 票反对、28 票弃权获得通过。 太平洋岛屿学生应对气候变化主任维沙尔·普拉萨德（Vishal Prasad）是发起国际法院咨询意见的学生之一。 “这必定是对破坏气候的责任追究的一个转折点，”他说。 “像太平洋地区一样，前线的社区已经等待太久，并继续为其他人的行为付出过高的代价。” 澳大利亚气候委员会首席执行官阿曼达·麦肯齐表示，这一裁决暴露了联邦政府对化石燃料出口的立场。 “虽然政府正在加大可再生能源发电的力度，但它仍然在给化石燃料巨头搭便车，”她说。 “继续大规模的新煤炭和天然气项目会让我们孩子的未来面临风险，现在显然违反了国际法。” 尽管追求大幅国内减排和雄心勃勃的可再生能源目标，但该国仍然是煤炭和天然气的主要出口国。 其他大型化石燃料生产国，包括美国、俄罗斯、伊朗和沙特阿拉伯，反对这项措施。 澳大利亚并不在该决议的 69 个共同提案国之列。澳大利亚和新西兰是唯一未出现在该名单中的太平洋国家。 澳大利亚在即将于土耳其举行的下一次缔约方大会气候变化谈判中担任关键的谈判主席，斐济和图瓦卢将举行正式的会前会议。 由于海平面上升，地势低洼的图瓦卢预计到本世纪末将失去 90% 的土地。 联合国大会决议正式重申了国际法院的调查结果，并敦促各国政府调整政策，将全球变暖幅度限制在 1.5 摄氏度以内。 它还敦促违规国家提供损害赔偿，并呼吁对化石燃料公司进行监管。 如需了解 SBS 新闻的最新动态，请下载我们的应用程序并订阅我们的时事通讯。

reflection.en: This news highlights the tension between economic interests and the call for environmental responsibility. Psalm 24:1 reminds us that the earth and everything in it belongs to 雅伟, inviting us to consider our role as stewards rather than ultimate owners. Our actions today have lasting impacts on the planet entrusted to our care.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻凸显了经济利益与环境责任之间的张力。诗篇24:1提醒我们，大地和其中所充满的都属于雅伟，这邀请我们思考自己作为管家而非最终所有者的角色。我们今天的行动对托付给我们的地球有着持久的影响。

verse.textEn: The earth is Yahweh's, and everything in it, the world, and all who live in it.
verse.textZh: 地和其中所充满的，世界和住在其间的，都属雅伟。

title.en: Israel envoy says Ben-Gvir not reflective of country, as activist treatment condemned
title.zh: 黄英贤谴责以色列拘留活动人士的待遇“令人震惊且不可接受”

summary.en: Australian Foreign Minister Penny Wong condemned the treatment of activists detained by Israel as "shocking and unacceptable." Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu also stated that the treatment of the activists by Itamar Ben-Gvir was wrong.
summary.zh: 澳大利亚外交部长黄英贤谴责以色列对待被拘留活动人士的方式“令人震惊且不可接受”。以色列总理本雅明·内塔尼亚胡也表示，伊塔马尔·本-格维尔对待这些活动人士的做法是错误的。

body.en:
Israel's ambassador to Australia, Hillel Newman, has joined growing condemnation of the actions of Israel's far-right security minister Itamar Ben-Gvir after he posted a video overnight showing detained activists from a Gaza-bound aid flotilla kneeling with their hands tied and foreheads on the ground.

The video, shared on X by Ben-Gvir, has drawn international condemnation. It was published after Israeli forces intercepted the flotilla's vessels at sea and began detaining hundreds of foreign activists at the southern port of Ashdod.

Newman told journalists Ben-Gvir's actions had been broadly condemned by the Israeli government and were not reflective of the government.

"He does not reflect the values of the state of Israel. He has been condemned by the prime minister, by the foreign minister, the entire leadership of the state of Israel.

"A country is not measured by the actions of one politician, but how the government responds to actions which are disgraceful."

Newman said that because his actions had been condemned, debate around Ben-Gvir should be put aside "and we address the real issue, which is the flotilla itself".

He repeated claims made by the Israeli government that the flotilla was a "provocation".

Earlier, Foreign Minister Penny Wong said the images of Ben-Gvir were "shocking and unacceptable".

"We condemn the actions of Israeli Minister Ben-Gvir — who Australia has sanctioned — and the degrading actions of Israeli authorities towards those detained," she said in a statement.

"I have asked Australia's Ambassador to Israel to make representations to Israel, reiterating our call for the release of the detained Australians and for Israel to ensure no ill treatment of any detainees and to act in line with international obligations."

She said Newman had been called in to the Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade to "reinforce this message".

Flotilla organisers had called on Prime Minister Anthony Albanese to join international condemnation of the footage, calling on the government to summon or send home Israel's ambassador to Australia.

"We are deeply concerned for all 318 participants, the 11 courageous Australian friends and their families," the Australian delegation of the Global Sumud Flotilla said in a statement.

"There's absolutely no need or no place for it, and you know, when it comes to people who are engaged in that journey, obviously our departments tried to discourage people from going down that path, but having gone down that path, they should be treated humanely.

"I can only imagine what it's like to be a parent or a loved one of one of the people involved in that trip, and to see them treat them being treated that way, I think is deeply disappointing."

body.zh: 外交部长黄英贤谴责了以色列极右翼安全部长伊塔马尔·本·格维尔的行为，此前他隔夜发布了一段视频，显示来自加沙的船队中被拘留的活动人士双手被绑，额头着地跪着。 Ben-Gvir 在 X 上分享的这段视频引起了国际社会的谴责。这篇文章是在以色列军队在海上拦截该船队的船只并开始在南部阿什杜德港拘留数百名外国活动人士之后发表的。 她在一份声明中表示：“我们谴责以色列部长本-格维尔的行为——澳大利亚已对他实施制裁——以及以色列当局对被拘留者采取的有辱人格的行为。” “我已要求澳大利亚驻以色列大使向以色列提出交涉，再次呼吁释放被拘留的澳大利亚人，并呼吁以色列确保不虐待任何被拘留者，并按照国际义务行事。” 船队组织者呼吁总理安东尼·阿尔巴内斯加入国际社会对这段视频的谴责，并呼吁政府召见或遣返以色列驻堪培拉大使。 Global Sumud 船队澳大利亚代表团在一份声明中表示：“我们对所有 318 名参与者、11 位勇敢的澳大利亚朋友及其家人深表关切。” 视频标题为“欢迎来到以色列”，视频显示数十名活动人士被迫双手被绑、额头着地跪下。有时，可以听到以色列国歌的背景音乐。 视频还显示，本-格维尔在被拘留的活动人士中质问并挥舞着以色列国旗。 美国驻以色列大使迈克·哈卡比谴责他所说的“卑鄙行为”。 赫卡比在 X 上写道：“以色列每一位高级官员都对本·格维尔的卑鄙行为表示普遍的愤怒和谴责。舰队是愚蠢的噱头，但本·格维尔背叛了他国家的尊严。” 欧盟委员哈贾·拉赫比卜 (Hadja Lahbib) 也批评了本·格维尔 (Ben-Gvir)，他在 X 上表示，“任何人都不应该因为捍卫人类而受到惩罚”。 法国表示，已就本格维尔的“不可接受的行为”召见以色列大使，而马德里则谴责对活动人士的“可怕”待遇，并表示以色列临时代办也被召见以示抗议。 比利时因一段“令人深感不安”的视频而召见以色列大使。 加拿大总理马克·卡尼表示，“舰队上平民受到的恶劣待遇……是不可接受的”，并补充说外交部长已指示官员传唤以色列大使。 爱尔兰外交部长海伦·麦肯蒂表示，她对这段视频感到“震惊和震惊”，并要求立即释放这些活动人士，其中包括妹妹……

reflection.zh: 当掌权者承认其管辖下的人员受到不当对待时，这凸显了道德治理的至关重要性。先知耶利米提醒领袖们，他们负有神圣的使命，要秉行公义和正直，确保任何人都不受不法或暴力的对待。这一呼吁适用于所有人的待遇，特别是那些弱势或被拘留的人。

title.en: Russia and China condemn US over indictment of former Cuban leader
title.zh: 俄罗斯和中国谴责美国起诉古巴前领导人

summary.en: It comes after the US charged Raúl Castro with murder, the latest move putting pressure on the regime.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
China and Russia have condemned a US decision to charge Cuba's former president Raúl Castro with murder.

The Chinese foreign ministry called on the US to stop using "coercion" and "threats" against its ally, while the Kremlin said the pressure being exerted on Havana "borders on violence".

The US has accused Castro over the 1996 downing of two planes, an incident that killed four people and fuelled diplomatic tensions between Washington and the Caribbean island.

US President Donald Trump has repeatedly sought to exert pressure on Cuba and has openly discussed toppling its communist regime.

The US has imposed fresh sanctions on the country and imposed an effective blockade on oil shipments to Cuba, exacerbating a fuel crisis there and leading to extended blackouts and food shortages.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov told Russian state media on Thursday that the US pressure campaign against Russia's long-time ally, including the indictment Castro, "cannot be condoned".

"We believe that under no circumstances should such methods - which border on violence - be used against either former or current heads of state," he added.

Chinese foreign ministry spokesman Guo Jiakun had earlier said the US should "stop threatening force at every turn", and that Beijing "firmly supports Cuba".

He said Beijing opposed "any attempt by external forces to exert pressure on Cuba under any pretext".

Guo continued: "The United States should cease using sanctions and judicial apparatus as tools of coercion against Cuba and refrain from making threats of force at every turn."

Castro was charged alongside five others on Wednesday over their alleged involvement in the shooting down of the two planes, which had been travelling between Cuba and Florida when they were struck.

The aircraft, which were operated by the Cuban-American dissident group Brothers to the Rescue, had been carrying three US citizens when they were downed, all of whom were killed.

At the time, Castro - who stepped down as president in 2018 - was head of the country's armed forces.

The incident caused outcry among Cuban exiles living in the US and has long been a source of contention between Washington and Havana.

Cuba's President Miguel Díaz-Canel has described the charges as "a political manoeuvre, devoid of any legal foundation".

Since capturing former Venezuelan President Nicolás Maduro in January, Trump has openly mused that Cuba was "ready to fall" .

It was a federal indictment against the left-wing authoritarian Maduro that was used by the Trump administration as its justification for its raid on the Venezuelan capital, Caracas, to seize him and his wife, Cilia Flores. The pair are now due to stand trial in New York on charges including drug trafficking.

title.en: New Chinese surveillance leaves foreigners nowhere to hide
title.zh: 中国新的监控让外国人无处藏身

summary.en: A Chinese cybersecurity expert has revealed to DW details of China's new high-tech policing. From ski resort facial recognition to seats on a train, the system can track anyone and compile a "holistic profile."

body.en:
A Chinese cybersecurity expert has revealed to DW details of China's new high-tech policing. From ski resort facial recognition to seats on a train, the system can track anyone and compile a "holistic profile."

When a cybersecurity researcher known by the pseudonym NetAskari recently clicked on a tab labeled "Inquiry for journalist files" on an unsecured Chinese web dashboard, he expected to see a jumble of auto-generated mock data.

Instead, familiar faces popped up on the screen. It was a comprehensive database of almost every foreign journalist based in the Chinese capital Beijing around 2021, including official passport photos taken at the entry/exit bureau, private cell phone numbers, visa details, and dates of birth. He also found his own exact personal information lying dormant on this Chinese police watchlist.

"It was more interesting than shocking," NetAskari told DW. "When you work as a journalist in China , you basically assume you are always on their radar. But what surprised me was simply how easy it was to access this highly sensitive system."

What NetAskari had stumbled upon is part modern China's emerging system of "holographic profiles."

He had unwittingly accessed a demonstration version of a remote tracking system designed for the Public Security Bureau in Zhangjiakou, the Hebei province city that hosted the 2022 Winter Olympics.

Though it was only a test panel, it was populated with real datasets, clearly outlining the trajectory of China's state surveillance machine, which is rapidly evolving from a network of simple street cameras into a data-fused, 24/7, predictive social control behemoth.

For years, China has operated the world's most extensive CCTV network. A massive initiative known as the "Xueliang" (Bright Eyes) project aims to merge these isolated islands of surveillance spread across the country.

But the data on the Zhangjiakou police dashboard shows the granular detail with which authorities can track an individual.

This system no longer relies solely on police cameras on street corners. It accurately records the specific train carriage and seat number a target occupies when arriving from Beijing or Shanghai.

It even synchronizes photos taken by facial-recognition ticket gates at local ski resorts directly into its tracking mechanism. The movements of the researcher's acquaintances who recently skied in Zhangjiakou were precisely flagged and mapped out with detailed trajectories in the system.

"The idea is simply to process as much data as possible from as many sensors as possible in real time," the researcher noted.

The system logs daily behaviors like gasoline consumption, regular shopping locations, and whether an individual frequently visits "petition areas."

title.en: Trump says he will speak to Taiwan's president in break from protocol
title.zh: 特朗普称他将违反礼节与台湾总统通话

summary.en: It comes as the US weighs whether to proceed with a $14bn arms sales to Taiwan, which China claims as its own.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
US President Donald Trump says he will talk to Taiwanese leader Lai Ching-te about a possible arms sale, in what would be a sharp departure from diplomatic tradition.

US and Taiwanese leaders have not spoken directly since 1979 - when Washington severed formal ties with Taiwan to recognise the Chinese government in Beijing.

China claims Taiwan as its territory and has not ruled out taking it by force. The US has long supported the self-ruled island and is bound by law to provide it with a means of self-defence, but has balanced this with maintaining diplomatic relations with China.

As president-elect in 2016, Trump took a phone call from Taiwan's then leader Tsai Ing-wen, angering Beijing.

President Lai, who took office in 2024, is behind one of the strongest pushes in years to strengthen the island's defence.

When asked on Wednesday if he planned to speak to Lai ahead of making a decision on US arms sales, Trump said: "I'll speak to him. I speak to everybody.. we'll work on that, the Taiwan problem."

He also hailed his relationship with China's President Xi as "amazing", on the back of a two-day summit in Beijing last week.

When asked about the potential conversation between Trump and Lai, a Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson said on Thursday that China "firmly opposes official exchanges between the United States and Taiwan", as well as US arms sales to Taiwan.

China urges the US to "stop sending wrong signals to the separatist forces in Taiwan," the spokesperson said.

In 1979, the US passed the Taiwan Relations Act which states that the US can "provide Taiwan with arms of a defensive character" - which is why it continues to sell weapons to Taiwan.

Trump has said he has yet to decide if the sale of a $14bn (£10.4bn) arms package to Taiwan, reportedly including anti-drone equipment and air-defence missile systems, will go ahead.

According to a report by the Financial Times, Beijing is currently holding up a proposed visit by the Pentagon's top policy official, Elbridge Colby - saying it cannot approve a visit until Trump decides how he will proceed with the arms deal.

Last week, while flying back from Beijing on Air Force One after his meeting with President Xi, Trump was similarly asked about weapons sales to Taiwan, to which he said he would "make a determination over the next fairly short period".

"I have to speak to the person that right now is, you know who he is, that's running Taiwan," he said.

During Trump's visit to Beijing, China had made it clear that Taiwan was one of the biggest issues in its relationship with the US, with Xi warning of "conflict" between the two superpowers if handled poorly.

title.en: Taiwan: Trump prods China with offer of direct Taipei talks
title.zh: 台湾：特朗普提议与台北直接对话，以此刺激中国

summary.en: Donald Trump has indicated he would engage in direct talks with Taiwan's president regarding the purchase of US arms. This action would deviate from established diplomatic norms of over four decades and is expected to be perceived as a challenge by China.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，他将与台湾领导人就购买美国武器进行直接对话。此举将打破四十多年的外交惯例，并可能被中国视为一种冒犯。

body.en:
Donald Trump has said he will talk with Taiwan's president about purchasing US arms. The move would break over four decades of protocol and be an affront to China.

US President Donald Trump on Wednesday reiterated his intention to hold direct talks with Taiwan 's President Lai Ching-te over a reported $14 billion (€12 billion) arms deal — the first direct talks between the presidents of both countries in over four decades.

"I'll speak to him. I speak to everybody," said Trump when asked about the situation.

Taiwan's Foreign Ministry said on Thursday that Lai would be "happy to discuss these matters with President Trump."

It added that Lai is "committed to maintaining the stable status quo in the Taiwan Strait."

Trump's statement was the second such made since his state visit to China last week.

The US leader previously said he had "a great meeting" with Chinese President Xi Jinping , adding, "We'll work on that… the Taiwan problem."

The US officially shifted Taiwanese diplomatic recognition from Taipei (the Republic of China, or ROC) to Beijing (the People's Republic of China, or PRC) in 1979 as part of its "One China" policy of strategic ambiguity and has not engaged in public presidential communications with Taiwanese leaders since that time.

That same year, the US also established the Taiwan Relations Act, committing itself by law to providing Taiwan with the means to defend itself against regional threats.

Although the US has continued to engage in backchannel talks with Taiwan, public displays of support from Washington are frowned upon by Beijing, which considers the self-governing democracy part of its territory and has threatened to take the island republic by force if necessary.

During Trump's recent state visit, China's Xi made clear that the handling of the Taiwan issue would be key to maintaining stability in US-China relations, warning that missteps could lead to an "extremely dangerous situation."

Trump has suggested US arms sales could be used as a bargaining chip with Beijing on the issue.

A spokesperson for the Chinese Foreign Ministry urged Trump to "handle the Taiwan issue with extreme caution and stop sending wrong signals to the separatist forces of Taiwan independence."

Taiwan is heavily reliant on US arms to deter China and is eager to double down on the $11 billion deal approved by the Trump administration in December.
body.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普表示，他将与台湾总统讨论购买美国武器的问题。此举将打破四十多年来的协议，是对中国的侮辱。 美国总统唐纳德·特朗普周三重申，他打算与台湾总统赖清德就一项据报道价值 140 亿美元（120 亿欧元）的军火交易进行直接会谈，这是四十多年来两国总统之间的首次直接会谈。 当被问及情况时，特朗普说：“我会和他说话。我会和每个人说话。” 台湾外交部周四表示，赖清德将“很乐意与特朗普总统讨论这些问题”。 声明补充说，黎智英“致力于维持台湾海峡的稳定现状”。 这是特朗普自上周对中国进行国事访问以来第二次发表此类声明。 这位美国领导人此前曾表示，他与中国国家主席习近平进行了“一次精彩的会面”，并补充道，“我们将致力于解决台湾问题。” 作为其“一个中国”战略模糊政策的一部分，美国于 1979 年正式将与台湾的外交承认从台北（中华民国，简称 ROC）转向北京（中华人民共和国，简称中华人民共和国），并且从那时起就没有与台湾领导人进行公开的总统沟通。 同年，美国还制定了《与台湾关系法》，依法承诺为台湾提供防御地区威胁的手段。 尽管美国继续与台湾进行秘密谈判，但北京方面对华盛顿公开表示支持表示不满，北京认为自治民主是其领土的一部分，并威胁在必要时以武力占领这个岛国。 在特朗普最近的国事访问期间，中国国家主席习近平明确表示，处理台湾问题是维护美中关系稳定的关键，并警告说，失误可能导致“极其危险的局面”。 特朗普表示，美国的军售可以作为在这个问题上与北京讨价还价的筹码。 中国外交部发言人敦促特朗普“高度谨慎处理台湾问题，停止向台独分裂势力发出错误信号”。 台湾严重依赖美国武器来威慑中国，并渴望加倍落实特朗普政府去年 12 月批准的 110 亿美元协议。

reflection.en: International relations often involve navigating complex protocols and sensitivities to maintain stability. The biblical call to "live at peace with everyone, as far as it depends on you," reminds leaders and nations of the ongoing responsibility to seek harmonious coexistence. title.en: Trump claims he will speak to Taiwan’s president, departing from decades-long diplomatic norms
title.zh: 特朗普声称将与台湾总统通话，打破数十年外交惯例

summary.en: Donald Trump announced his intention to speak with Taiwan's President Lai Ching-te, a move that would break decades of US diplomatic practice since Washington recognized Beijing in 1979 and could lead to significant international tension.
summary.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普宣布他打算与台湾总统赖清德通话，此举将打破自1979年华盛顿承认北京以来美国数十年来的外交惯例，并可能导致重大的国际紧张局势。

body.en: US and Taiwanese presidents have not spoken directly since Washington shifted diplomatic recognition to Beijing from Taipei in 1979 Donald Trump said on Wednesday he would speak to Taiwan’s President Lai Ching-te, an unprecedented move for a US leader that could roil US relations with China. “I’ll speak to him,” the US president told reporters at Joint Base Andrews in Maryland before boarding Air Force One when asked about Lai. “I speak to everybody … We’ll work on that, the Taiwan problem.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 自1979年华盛顿从台北转而与北京建立外交关系以来，美国和台湾总统就没有直接说过话。唐纳德·特朗普周三表示，他将与台湾地区领导人赖清德通话，这对美国领导人来说是史无前例的举动，可能会扰乱美国与中国的关系。当被问及赖智时，美国总统在登上空军一号之前在马里兰州安德鲁斯联合基地对记者说：“我会和他谈谈。” “我对每个人都说过……我们将致力于解决台湾问题。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: Major diplomatic shifts, especially those departing from long-standing norms, carry significant weight for international stability. Proverbs 11:14 reminds us that a nation's well-being often depends on wise counsel and careful guidance. In complex global affairs, seeking broad wisdom can help navigate potential challenges and foster peaceful relations.
reflection.zh: 重大的外交转变，特别是那些偏离长期惯例的举动，对国际稳定具有重要影响。箴言11:14提醒我们，国家的福祉往往取决于明智的忠告和审慎的指导。在全球复杂的事务中，寻求广泛的智慧有助于应对潜在挑战并促进和平关系。

verse.textEn: For lack of guidance a nation falls, but victory is won through many advisers.
verse.textZh: 无智谋，民就败落；谋士多，人便安居。

title.en: Nvidia’s revenue blows past Wall Street expectations as AI boom accelerates
title.zh: 英伟达营收远超华尔街预期，人工智能热潮加速发展

summary.en: Nvidia's revenue surpassed Wall Street's expectations, reinforcing investor confidence in the accelerating AI boom and its global expansion.
summary.zh: 英伟达的收入超出华尔街预期，进一步增强了投资者对人工智能（AI）热潮及其全球扩张的信心。

body.en: Many analysts view company’s financial performance as a broader referendum on AI buildout Nvidia continued its years-long streak of beating Wall Street’s expectations for growth on Wednesday, reassuring most investors that the AI boom, particularly the global explosion of datacenters, will continue apace. “The buildout of AI factories – the largest infrastructure expansion in human history – is accelerating at extraordinary speed,” said Nvidia’s CEO, Jensen Huang, in a statement . “Agentic AI has arrived, doing productive work, generating real value, and scaling rapidly across companies and industries.” Continue reading...
body.zh: 许多分析师将公司的财务表现视为对人工智能建设的更广泛的公投周三，英伟达延续了多年来超出华尔街增长预期的势头，让大多数投资者放心，人工智能的繁荣，特别是全球数据中心的爆炸式增长，将继续快速发展。英伟达首席执行官黄仁勋在一份声明中表示：“人工智能工厂的建设——人类历史上最大规模的基础设施扩张——正在以惊人的速度加速。” “代理人工智能已经到来，它可以做富有成效的工作，产生真正的价值，并在公司和行业中快速扩展。”继续阅读...

reflection.en: The rapid acceleration of the AI boom, reflected in Nvidia's financial success, highlights a remarkable increase in human knowledge and technological capability. This era of expanding information reminds us of ancient prophecies that spoke of a time when knowledge would increase.
reflection.zh: 英伟达的财务成功所反映出的人工智能热潮的迅速加速，凸显了人类知识和技术能力的显著增长。这个信息不断扩展的时代，让我们想起古老的预言，其中提到知识将会增加的时刻。

verse.textEn: But you, Daniel, roll up and seal the words of the scroll until the time of the end. Many will go here and there to increase knowledge.
verse.textZh: 但以理啊，你要隐藏这话，封闭这书，直到末时。必有多人来往奔跑，知识就必增长。

title.en: Rosenberg: Putin enjoys Xi's Chinese welcome but heads home without pipeline deal
title.zh: 罗森伯格：普京受到习近平的中国欢迎，但未达成管道协议就回国

summary.en: Russia and China showed they were shoulder-to-shoulder on the world stage, but it became clear there are limits, says the BBC's Russia Editor.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自中国栏目的新闻，重点涉及和平与克制。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
As Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping walked the red carpet towards the Great Hall of the People, a Chinese military band played the romantic Russian classic Moscow Nights.

It was the language of two leaders who like to show they've built a special relationship. They have had plenty of time to do so: they have met more than 40 times over the years.

In their public statements they spoke of "strategic co-operation" between their nations, about "partnership", "mutual respect", "friendship" and "trust."

Together they railed against the "irresponsible" nuclear policy of the United States and condemned Donald Trump's plan for a Golden Dome missile defence shield.

On the eve of the visit the Russian government newspaper had published two big photos on its front page: one of a lonely-looking Trump climbing the steps of Air Force One at the end of his China trip last week; and beside it an old image of Putin and Xi walking together.

The visual messaging was unmistakable: Russia and China are shoulder-to- shoulder on the world stage.

And in the world of geopolitics relationships are rarely based on love and affection. It's often self-interest.

Russia is keen to push ahead with plans for a new pipeline, Power of Siberia 2, and had hoped for progress in Beijing. The pipeline would bring additional volumes of Russian gas from Western Siberia to Northern China via Mongolia and, for Moscow, help make up for the loss of European markets.

Last year Russia and China had signed a memorandum of understanding on the project, but Beijing appears in no rush to do the deal. As well as pricing issues, some commentators believe China wants to avoid over-dependence on Russian fossil fuels.

On Wednesday the Kremlin said Russia and China had reached a "general understanding on the parameters" of the project.

"The positions of Russia and China are not identical. Their interests do not always coincide," the Russian government newspaper had conceded: the same edition that had published the photo of Putin and Xi side-by-side.

"With two countries of this size, both with a great-power psyche, it couldn't be any other way."

It wasn't so long ago that the word "bromance" was being applied to another high-level relationship: this time Putin-Trump, as Russia and America pledged to thaw ties.

After the two presidents met in Alaska last summer Russian officials began referring to "the spirit of Anchorage" and hinting that Moscow and Washington had reached a mutual understanding on how to end the war in Ukraine (on terms acceptable to Moscow).

"The spirit of Beijing exists," Putin's foreign policy aide Yuri Ushakov said on the sidelines of the summit.
body.zh: 当弗拉基米尔·普京和习近平走上红地毯走向人民大会堂时，中国军乐队演奏了浪漫的俄罗斯经典《莫斯科之夜》。 这是两位领导人想要表明他们已经建立了特殊关系的语言。他们有充足的时间这样做：这些年来他们已经会面了 40 多次。 他们在公开声明中谈到了两国之间的“战略合作”、“伙伴关系”、“相互尊重”、“友谊”和“信任”。 他们共同谴责美国“不负责任”的核政策，并谴责唐纳德·特朗普的金顶导弹防御系统计划。 访问前夕，俄罗斯政府报纸在头版刊登了两张大照片：一张是特朗普上周结束中国之行时，一脸孤独地爬上空军一号的台阶；一张是特朗普在访问中国期间，一脸孤独地爬上空军一号的台阶；一张是特朗普在中国访问结束后，一脸孤独地爬上空军一号的台阶；一张是特朗普在访问中国期间，一脸孤独地爬上空军一号的台阶。旁边是普京和习近平一起散步的老照片。 视觉信息是明确无误的：俄罗斯和中国在世界舞台上并肩作战。 在地缘政治世界中，关系很少是建立在爱和感情的基础上的。这往往是出于自身利益。 俄罗斯热衷于推进新管道“西伯利亚力量2号”的计划，并希望北京能够取得进展。该管道将​​把更多的俄罗斯天然气从西西伯利亚经蒙古输送到中国北部，对于莫斯科来说，有助于弥补欧洲市场的损失。 去年，俄罗斯和中国就该项目签署了谅解备忘录，但北京方面似乎并不急于达成协议。除了定价问题外，一些评论人士认为，中国希望避免过度依赖俄罗斯化石燃料。 克里姆林宫周三表示，俄罗斯和中国已就该项目的“参数达成总体谅解”。 俄罗斯政府报纸承认：“俄罗斯和中国的立场并不相同。他们的利益并不总是一致的。”该报纸还刊登了普京和习近平并肩的照片。 “对于两个如此规模的国家，都具有大国心态，没有其他办法了。” 不久前，“兄弟情谊”这个词还被应用于另一种高层关系：这次是普京与特朗普，俄罗斯和美国承诺解冻关系。 去年夏天两国总统在阿拉斯加会晤后，俄罗斯官员开始提及“安克雷奇精神”，并暗示莫斯科和华盛顿已就如何结束乌克兰战争达成了共同谅解（以莫斯科可接受的条件）。 “北京精神是存在的，”普京的外交政策助手尤里·乌沙科夫在峰会间隙表示。

reflection.en: This story draws attention to peace-making and restraint. Matthew 5:9 reminds us to meet sharp headlines with mercy, truth, and restraint, asking how faithful people can respond with wisdom instead of noise.
reflection.zh: 这则新闻让人想到和平与克制。Matthew 5:9提醒我们，在快速变化的新闻里，仍要以怜悯、真实与节制来回应，并学习用祷告与分辨代替情绪化判断。

title.en: 'My dear friend': Putin and Xi praise partnership during talks in Beijing
title.zh: “我亲爱的朋友”：普京与习近平在北京会谈中赞扬伙伴关系

summary.en: While Russia faces economic and financial sanctions from other countries, China remains a prominent and loyal customer.
summary.zh: 尽管俄罗斯面临其他国家的经济和金融制裁，中国仍然是其重要的忠实客户。

body.en:
Russian President Vladimir Putin has lauded his close ties with Chinese leader Xi Jinping, saying the nations are partners in trade and international affairs during bilateral talks in Beijing.

Xi welcomed Putin with a ceremony at the Great Hall of the People only days after meeting United States President Donald Trump.

The quick succession of Trump's and Putin's visits highlighted China's growing role as an international superpower, experts say.

Putin greeted Xi warmly as they met for the bilateral talks, describing the Chinese president as a "dear friend".

"We are truly delighted to see you. We keep in constant touch, both personally and through our aides in the government," he said.

Xi also stressed the "political mutual trust and strategic co-operation" between the countries, according to Chinese state media.

The two leaders have praised each other profusely in the past — Xi once describing Putin as his "best and most intimate friend".

Xi and Putin were set to focus on energy and security as well as their overall ties.

Chinese state media reported both parties agreed to extend a friendship treaty first signed in 2001.

China became Russia's top trading partner after Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022.

China has said it is neutral in the conflict, maintaining trade ties with Russia despite economic and financial sanctions against Russia by the US and Europe.

China is the top customer for Russian oil and gas supplies, and Russia expects the war in Iran to increase the demand.

"The driving force behind economic co-operation is Russian-Chinese collaboration in the energy sector," Putin said.

"Amid the crisis in the Middle East, Russia continues to maintain its role as a reliable supplier of resources, while China remains a responsible consumer of these resources."

Xi stressed the need for the "complete cessation of hostilities" in the Middle East, according to Chinese state media.

"An early end to the conflict will help reduce disruptions to energy supply stability, the smooth flow of industrial and supply chains, and international trade order," Xi said.

A Russian presidential aide said earlier that Russia's oil exports to China grew by 35 per cent in the first quarter of 2026. Russia was also one of the biggest exporters of natural gas to China.

Putin said China and Russia's co-operation in foreign policy is "one of the key stabilising factors on the international stage".

In February 2022, just weeks before Russia invaded Ukraine, China and Russia announced a "no limits" partnership during a trip by Putin to Beijing.

Despite taking a neutral stance in the conflict, China supports Russia through frequent state visits, growing trade and joint military drills.

title.en: EV battery supply chains in focus as China halts sulphuric acid exports
title.zh: 中国暂停硫酸出口，电动汽车电池供应链受关注

summary.en: China's decision to stop exporting sulphuric acid is expected to create pressure on global supply chains for both electric vehicle batteries and fertilizers.
summary.zh: 中国停止出口硫酸预计将对电动汽车电池和化肥的全球供应链造成压力。

body.en:
China has banned exports of sulphuric acid, the world's most used industrial chemical and a crucial ingredient in battery and clothing manufacturing, as well as fertiliser production and metal processing industries.

The move comes amid pressures on supply of the chemical after conflict in the Middle East disrupted sulphur shipments through the Strait of Hormuz earlier this year.

Marina Zhang from the University of Technology Sydney's Australia-China Relations Institute said that, while the ban may have been presented by China as temporary, it signals a policy shift from Australia's largest trading partner towards increasingly prioritising control over industrial inputs.

"It's not just finished products, but the upstream materials, processing technologies and basic industrial ingredients that allow advanced manufacturing to scale … So while the immediate measure may be temporary, the underlying logic is structural," Zhang told SBS News.

Sulphur is the primary ingredient used to produce sulphuric acid, meaning shipping and processing delays of the raw material in the Gulf region have created flow-on effects for manufacturers reliant on a steady supply.

In 2025, about half of the global seaborne supply of sulphur came from the Middle East.

China accounted for a significant share of sulphuric acid shipments from Asia last year and remains one of the world's largest exporters. The loss of that supply is now raising concerns among overseas buyers already scrambling to secure alternative sources.

While the impacts are expected to be spread across multiple industries, analysts say battery supply chains could be among the most exposed.

Zhang said the situation "reveals a paradox at the heart of the clean-energy transition … which depends on minerals that require very energy-intensive, chemical-intensive and often environmentally difficult processing".

"Yet many Western countries have spent decades outsourcing precisely those 'dirty' industrial activities."

Sulphuric acid also plays an important role in processing metals such as nickel and copper, both used extensively in electric vehicle batteries and energy storage systems.

Indonesia's rapidly expanding nickel-processing industry is considered particularly vulnerable to the bans.

The country has become a major producer of battery-grade nickel used in global electric vehicle (EV) supply chains, including by manufacturers linked to Chinese battery maker CATL.

Refining lower-grade nickel ores into battery materials requires large volumes of sulphuric acid for a process known as high-pressure acid leaching.

body.zh: 中国已禁止出口硫酸，硫酸是世界上使用最广泛的工业化学品，也是电池和服装制造、化肥生产和金属加工业的关键成分。 今年早些时候，中东冲突扰乱了通过霍尔木兹海峡的硫磺运输，导致化学品供应面临压力。 悉尼科技大学澳中关系研究所的玛丽娜·张表示，虽然中国提出的禁令可能是暂时的，但它标志着澳大利亚最大贸易伙伴的政策转变，越来越优先考虑对工业投入的控制。 “这不仅仅是成品，还有上游材料、加工技术和基本工业原料，使先进制造业能够规模化……因此，虽然眼前的措施可能是暂时的，但潜在的逻辑是结构性的，”张告诉SBS新闻。 硫是用于生产硫酸的主要成分，这意味着海湾地区原材料的运输和加工延迟对依赖稳定供应的制造商产生了连锁效应。 到 2025 年，全球海运硫磺供应量的一半左右来自中东。 去年，中国占亚洲硫酸出口量的很大一部分，并且仍然是世界最大的出口国之一。这种供应的损失现在引起了已经在争相寻找替代来源的海外买家的担忧。 虽然预计影响将波及多个行业，但分析师表示，电池供应链可能是受影响最大的行业之一。 张说，这种情况“揭示了清洁能源转型核心的一个悖论……这取决于需要能源密集型、化学密集型且通常对环境困难的加工的矿物”。 “然而，许多西方国家花费了数十年的时间，将那些‘肮脏’的工业活动外包出去。” 硫酸在镍和铜等金属加工中也发挥着重要作用，这两种金属广泛用于电动汽车电池和储能系统。 印度尼西亚快速扩张的镍加工业被认为特别容易受到禁令的影响。 中国已成为全球电动汽车（EV）供应链中使用的电池级镍的主要生产国，其中包括与中国电池制造商宁德时代相关的制造商。 将低品位镍矿石精炼成电池材料需要大量硫酸，这一过程被称为高压酸浸出。 如果供应仍然受到限制，炼油厂可能面临更高的生产成本、延误和原料竞争加剧，并可能流向电池制造商和电动汽车……

title.en: Neo-nazi group lodge legal challenge against hate group listing

summary.en: Thomas Sewell, leader of neo-nazi group White Australia, said the injunction seeks to stop the government from using "legislation to arrest or imprison" him.
summary.zh: 这是一则来自澳洲栏目的新闻，重点涉及领导、智慧与公共责任。如需完整细节，请阅读英文原始报道。

body.en:
Neo-Nazi organisation White Australia's bid for temporary immunity from being listed as an illegal hate group has been put on ice — but the High Court could decide the matter as soon as June.

The group, previously known as the National Socialist Network, is seeking to overturn the government's hate speech legislation and wants an injunction to effectively block the home affairs minister from outlawing it.

"The aim of the injunction is to prevent the government from using this legislation to arrest or imprison me while the High Court determines this legislation's constitutional validity," top neo-Nazi Thomas Sewell, who lodged the case, said in a post on Telegram ahead of the hearing.

But High Court Justice Jayne Jagot said the bid was not urgent and could be dealt with at a hearing in coming weeks.

"Mr Sewell had been on notice that the White Australia Party was likely to be specified a prohibited hate group," she said during a directions hearing on Thursday.

"The circumstances on which the party relied for interlocutory relief ... were of its own making."

The next hearing will be held between 2 June and 5 June, when the application to block the listing could be decided.

A two-day final hearing at which the constitutionality of the hate speech legislation will be discussed is scheduled for early September.

White Australia has been seeking to establish itself as a political force aiming to run in the next federal election.

Asked whether he wanted the matter to be dealt with before the deadline for candidates to run in the 2026 Victorian election, White Australia's barrister Peter King said that was not critical.

"I'm instructed that the Victorian election deadline, as it were, is not critical ... the validity and entitlement of their political party ... is critical," he told the court.

After receiving advice from spy agency ASIO, Home Affairs Minister Tony Burke declared the neo-Nazi organisation a prohibited hate group under laws passed following the Bondi Beach terror attack.

White Australia's predecessor, the National Socialist Network, announced it was disbanding when the hate laws were introduced.

In reality, Mr Burke said, the group had "phoenixed" — changing its name to White Australia and continuing operations with largely the same members.

Under the government's declaration, it is now a crime to support, fund or join the group.

Islamist organisation Hizbut Tahrir has also been banned under the post-Bondi laws.
